title: Meetings and sharing (overview)
text: Start and join video meetings, manage people, share a file and hand control of it to someone else.

title: Meetings and sharing: Open your workspace
text: Open your workspace. Sign in and you land on your Workspace. The big tiles start or join a meeting, schedule one, edit and sign PDFs, or share your booking link. Pick More tools to add other tiles.

title: Meetings and sharing: Add tools to your workspace
text: Add tools to your workspace. Press More tools. Every tool is listed in groups (Meetings, Meeting records, Communication and more). Press Add to put a tool on your workspace. Remove it later with the × on its tile. Good to know: Webinars is in the Meetings group.

title: Meetings and sharing: Start a meeting
text: Start a meeting. Press Start a meeting. You see the lobby: a preview of your camera, your name, the meeting link and the Meeting ID. Copy the link and send it to people, then press Join. Good to know: In a shared open room, microphone and camera start off. Turn them on with the buttons when you are ready.

title: Meetings and sharing: Inside the meeting
text: Inside the meeting. The bar at the bottom has Mute, Camera, Share, People, Chat, React, Host tools, More and Leave. The host can change who may unmute or start video from the People panel.

title: Meetings and sharing: People and the arrow menu
text: People and the arrow menu. Press People. Next to each person, the small arrow before the microphone opens a menu: Chat, Ask to unmute, Ask to start video, Make co-host, Make host and Remove from meeting. Hosts see all of them; everyone else sees Chat. Good to know: Mute all and the two checkboxes at the bottom decide whether people can unmute or start video themselves.

title: Meetings and sharing: The More menu
text: The More menu. More holds the rest: captions, background, invite, record, share a link, share a file, whiteboard, notes and documents, breakout rooms and security. Pin the tools you use most.

title: Meetings and sharing: Share a file through iSift
text: Share a file through iSift. Open More and choose Share a file, then pick a PDF or a photo. iSift shows the file to everyone and you page through it with the arrows at the bottom. Use this instead of sharing your whole screen when you want to hand control to someone. For a PowerPoint or Word file, save it as a PDF first. Good to know: Only files shared through iSift can be controlled by another person. A shared screen or window cannot.

title: Meetings and sharing: Give control to a participant
text: Give control to a participant. While you share a file, a Give control to… list appears at the bottom left. Pick a person. They get a message, and everyone sees who has control.

title: Meetings and sharing: What the participant can do
text: What the participant can do. The participant sees a blue bar: You control the file, with Previous, Next, scroll up and scroll down. Their clicks move your shared file on every screen. Good to know: They can move and scroll the file. They cannot edit it, and they cannot stop your sharing.

title: Meetings and sharing: Take control back
text: Take control back. The shared page moved when the participant pressed Next. You can press Take back at any time. Only you can stop sharing, and control also returns to you when you stop sharing or either of you leaves.

title: Webinars (overview)
text: Run a webinar like Zoom or Webex: registration, panelists, a practice session, private questions, polls, letting people speak and reports.

title: Webinars: Open Webinars
text: Open Webinars. Go to Meetings and choose the Webinars tab. Your webinars are listed under Upcoming and Past. Press Schedule a webinar. Good to know: Webinars must be switched on in Admin Console, Customers, Modules, and allowed for your plan.

title: Webinars: Schedule the webinar
text: Schedule the webinar. Give it a title and description, a date, time and length. Add panelists (they speak and share like you). Choose whether people must register, whether you approve each one, and add extra questions. Set chat to go to you only, Q&A, raise hand, reminders and follow-up emails. Good to know: The chat default Goes to me only keeps attendee questions private.

title: Webinars: Share the registration page
text: Share the registration page. The webinar page shows the registration link and a personal link for each panelist. Copy the registration link and share it anywhere. Registered people and panelists are emailed their own links.

title: Webinars: Prepare polls
text: Prepare polls. Open the Polls tab and add questions with up to ten answers. You launch each poll from the room during the webinar.

title: Webinars: People register
text: People register. Attendees open your registration link, enter name and email (and any questions you added) and press Register. They receive a personal link by email.

title: Webinars: Attendees get their link
text: Attendees get their link. After registering, an attendee can press Open my personal link, then Join the webinar. They can also add it to their calendar from that page.

title: Webinars: Practice session
text: Practice session. With Practice session on, attendees wait on a holding screen until you press Go live. They can only watch: their microphone, camera and screen are always off.

title: Webinars: Host view before going live
text: Host view before going live. Open the webinar room. A banner shows the practice session and how many are waiting. Check your sound and camera with your panelists, then press Go live.

title: Webinars: Going live
text: Going live. Attendees are let in automatically. They see the host and speakers and a LIVE badge. They can use Q&A, Polls, React and Raise hand.

title: Webinars: Attendees ask questions
text: Attendees ask questions. In Q&A an attendee types a question and can ask anonymously. Questions go to the host and panelists, not to other attendees. Attendees can upvote public questions.

title: Webinars: Answer questions
text: Answer questions. In your Q&A panel, type an answer, press Answered live, dismiss or reopen. Filters show Open, Answered and All.

title: Webinars: Run a poll
text: Run a poll. Open Polls, press Launch poll, watch the votes arrive and choose whether to share the results with attendees.

title: Webinars: Let people speak
text: Let people speak. Open People. Tick one or several attendees and press Let N speak, or use Let speak on one person. They join the stage muted and unmute themselves. You can mute them, turn their video off, mute all speakers or move them back to watching. Good to know: Attendees who raised a hand appear at the top of the list.

title: Webinars: A speaker on the stage
text: A speaker on the stage. The invited person now appears in the Speaking list with their mute, video-off and Back to watching buttons.

title: Webinars: Reports and follow-up
text: Reports and follow-up. After the webinar open Reports: registered, attended, watch time, questions answered and poll votes. Download CSV files and send a thank-you to those who came or a note to those who missed it. Good to know: Follow-up emails go once to each person.

source: Manual: Booking, minutes and action items
title: Booking, minutes and action items (overview)
text: Let people book time with you, then turn each meeting into reviewed minutes, owned action items and a morning briefing.

source: Manual: Booking, minutes and action items
title: Booking, minutes and action items: Your booking page
text: Your booking page. Go to Meetings, Booking. Create a booking page, set your weekly hours, meeting length and notice. People pick a free time with no account and get a video link. Good to know: Mail must be connected for confirmation emails.

source: Manual: Booking, minutes and action items
title: Booking, minutes and action items: Meetings list and minutes
text: Meetings list and minutes. Meetings that have a transcript can have minutes drafted. Open Minutes to see each meeting and its status. Good to know: Minutes are drafts. A person reviews and approves them before they go out.

source: Manual: Booking, minutes and action items
title: Booking, minutes and action items: Action items
text: Action items. Action items from approved minutes appear here with an owner and a due date, so follow-up does not depend on someone's notebook.

source: Manual: Booking, minutes and action items
title: Booking, minutes and action items: Morning briefing
text: Morning briefing. Briefings prepare you for the day: what is on and what is still open. Use Preview to see one without sending it.

title: Mail, calendar and contacts (overview)
text: Use Commbox to read mail, keep your calendar and look after contacts beside your meetings.

title: Mail, calendar and contacts: Open Commbox
text: Open Commbox. Commbox has three tabs: Mail, Calendar and Contacts. With no account yet, press Add account.

title: Mail, calendar and contacts: Add a mail account
text: Add a mail account. Enter your email address and press Continue. iSift finds the settings for Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, Hotmail, Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. Or create an iSift address of your own, or use your own domain with team mailboxes. Good to know: Phones and Outlook or Thunderbird can be set up from the isiftmail page.

title: Mail, calendar and contacts: Your calendar
text: Your calendar. Calendar shows your meetings and events together. Use Today, Day, Week and Month, add a new event, and Sync to pull in Outlook or Google events.

title: Mail, calendar and contacts: Contacts
text: Contacts. Add contacts by hand, or bring them in from Outlook. People with an iSift account can be called or messaged from here.

source: Manual: Documents, PDF signing and whiteboard
title: Documents, PDF signing and whiteboard (overview)
text: Write, calculate, present, sign and sketch without leaving iSift.

source: Manual: Documents, PDF signing and whiteboard
title: Documents, PDF signing and whiteboard: WordPerfect documents
text: WordPerfect documents. Docs, WordPerfect. Press New to write with headings, lists, tables and links. Documents are private until you share them and save automatically.

source: Manual: Documents, PDF signing and whiteboard
title: Documents, PDF signing and whiteboard: SpreadTable spreadsheets
text: SpreadTable spreadsheets. SpreadTable works with formulas, several sheets and CSV import and export.

source: Manual: Documents, PDF signing and whiteboard
title: Documents, PDF signing and whiteboard: PowerPresentation slides
text: PowerPresentation slides. Make slides, present them in a meeting, print and share.

source: Manual: Documents, PDF signing and whiteboard
title: Documents, PDF signing and whiteboard: Sign and edit PDFs
text: Sign and edit PDFs. Choose a PDF or Word file, edit its text, delete or replace pictures, draw a signature or sign with your own certificate. The file stays in your browser and is not stored on the server. Good to know: PDFs of up to 5 pages are free.

source: Manual: Documents, PDF signing and whiteboard
title: Documents, PDF signing and whiteboard: Whiteboard
text: Whiteboard. Sketch ideas. Boards save automatically and can be shared in a meeting with everyone.

title: Administration (overview)
text: For administrators: set up the workspace, decide who can use what and keep integrations working.

title: Administration: Admin Console
text: Admin Console. Open Admin Console. The Setup checklist lists what still needs doing, such as the administrator password, mail sending and the video server.

title: Administration: People and plans
text: People and plans. Under Customers: Users (add, disable or delete people), Permissions, Plans, Modules and Mailboxes.

title: Administration: Switch modules on or off
text: Switch modules on or off. Modules lists every part of iSift, including Webinars. Untick one and it disappears from the menu, dashboard and home page for everyone. Good to know: Allow webinars for a single user under Users, Edit.

title: Administration: Meeting platforms
text: Meeting platforms. Connect Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Zoom and the video server for big meetings. Secrets are stored encrypted and shown masked.

title: One workspace, not six tabs
text: Video meetings, a Calendly-style booking page, mail, calendar and contacts, notes, whiteboard and PDF signing, all signed in once and all linked to the meeting they belong to.

title: Follow-through, not just a summary
text: Most tools stop at a recap. iSift turns the conversation into minutes, owned action items and a briefing before your next meeting.

title: AI-empowered, human-approved
text: Draft minutes and actions are marked for review. Nothing is sent as final until someone checks it, which matters for clients, boards and regulated work.

title: Booking pages built in
text: Share a link and let people pick a free time. Each booking lands in your calendar with a meeting room attached. No second subscription.

title: Edit and sign PDFs in the browser
text: Change text, add shapes, draw a signature, sign with your own certificate. The file is not stored on our servers.

title: A meeting screen that feels like Zoom
text: A clean toolbar with only what you need, and a More menu for the rest: pin the tools you use. Reactions, raise hand, live captions with a saveable transcript, waiting room, lock meeting and hide profile pictures. On a phone you are large on the first screen and everyone else swipes in after.

title: Share together, point and draw
text: Share a whole screen, one window or one browser tab, with its sound. Let several people share at once, side by side, and hand someone the pen to point and draw on your screen, then take it back.

title: Watch a video together
text: Paste a YouTube link and everyone watches in sync on their own device, phones included. You play, pause and skip for the whole meeting.

title: Meeting rooms people enjoy
text: A virtual boardroom with a wooden table, name plates, windows and your own background, or a simple gallery view. Switch with one button.

title: Call a teammate in one click
text: Ring another iSift user like a phone call. They accept and you are in a private room together.

title: Webinars you run like Zoom or Webex
text: Registration pages with your own questions, panelists, a practice session before you go live, and attendees who can only watch. You mute people or turn their video off, and invite one person or a group to speak. Attendee questions come to you privately, with Q&A, upvotes, polls and raise hand. Afterwards get attendance, question and poll reports as CSV, and send follow-up emails.

title: Your own email address, set up in minutes
text: Get a name@isift address or use your own domain with mailboxes for your team. Phones and Outlook or Thunderbird are set up from one page, with built-in spam and abuse protection, inside the same Commbox as your calendar and contacts.

title: You stay in control
text: Basic hosts save recordings on their own computer when the meeting ends; paid plans store them in the cloud and email a download link. Administrators set what each person may use: call time, recording, documents, Commbox and more.

title: Plain, local pricing
text: Free, Standard and Business. Pick how many participants you need from a dropdown, in your currency, and yearly saves you money. No per-feature add-ons to work out.

title: Webinars
text: Registration pages, panelists, a practice session, view-only attendees, private questions to the host, Q&A with upvotes, polls, raise hand, reports and follow-up emails.

title: Give control of a shared file
text: Share a PDF or photo through iSift and hand one person the controls: they page and scroll it for everyone. You take it back, or stop sharing, at any time.

title: Your own email address
text: An iSift address in minutes, or your own domain with team mailboxes, set up on phones and in Outlook or Thunderbird from one page.

title: Host controls that stay out of the way
text: Mute people or turn off their video, invite one person or a group to speak, and a small arrow beside each person holds Chat, Ask to unmute and more.

title: Encrypted connection
text: All traffic uses HTTPS. Passwords are stored as salted hashes, and saved API keys are encrypted.

title: Recordings stay with you
text: Basic hosts save the recording on their own computer when the meeting ends. On paid plans it is stored in the cloud and a download link is emailed to the host.

title: Your files are not kept
text: PDFs you edit or sign are processed for your request and sent straight back. They are not stored.

title: A person approves the AI
text: Minutes and action items are drafts until someone reviews them. The Privacy page lists every provider we use and what it does.

title: Everything in one place
text: Zoom, Zoho, Teams, Webex, GoTo and Meet each cover meetings; notes, whiteboard, documents, PDF signing, booking and mail usually mean other apps or add-ons. In iSift they sit beside the meeting.

title: Webinars are included
text: Webinars are a separate product or an add-on with Zoom, Zoho, GoTo and Teams. In iSift they are part of the paid plans, with registration, Q&A, polls and reports.

title: You pay for the people you need
text: Choose how many participants you need from a dropdown. No per-feature add-ons to work out.

title: A free plan with 90-minute meetings
text: Group meetings on the free plan run for 90 minutes, longer than the free plans of Zoom, Webex and Meet.

title: AI that a person approves
text: Minutes and action items are drafts until someone reviews them, which matters for clients, boards and regulated work.

title: Control without installing anything
text: Share a file and give someone control of it, mute and manage people and run a webinar, all in the browser.

title: Webinars: For the host (Meetings > Webinars)
text: 1. **Schedule a webinar**: title, description, date and length, panelists, registration (automatic or manual approval, capacity, extra questions), chat mode, Q&A and reminder options. 2. Share the **registration page** (`#/webinar/<id>`). Each registrant gets an email with a personal link; panelists get their own links and a calendar file. 3. Open the room early. With *Practice session* on, attendees wait on a holding screen until you press **Go live**. 4. In the room, the **Q&A** panel has three tabs: Q&A, Polls and People. 5. After it ends: Reports (registered, attended, watch time, questions, poll votes), CSV downloads, and follow-up emails to those who came or missed it.

title: Webinars: Who can do what in the room
text: | Role | Hears / sees | Speaks | Chat | |---|---|---|---| | Host, panelist | everyone | yes | everyone | | Speaker (attendee the host invited) | everyone | yes, until moved back | as chat mode allows | | Attendee | the stage only | **never** (server enforces mic, camera and screen off) | per chat mode | - **Mute and video off**: mute or stop the video of any speaker, or *Mute all speakers* / *Mute and video off*. - **Let people speak**: tick one or many attendees and press *Let N speak*, or use *Let speak* on one person. They join the stage with the microphone muted and unmute themselves; you can mute them again at any time, and *Back to watching* returns them to view-only. - **Private questions**: the default chat mode is **Goes to the host only**. Attendee chat messages reach the host (and co-hosts) and are never shown to other attendees. Other modes: host and panelists, everyone, off. - **Q&A**: attendees ask (optionally anonymous), upvote; staff answer in writing, mark *answered live*, dismiss or reopen. Anonymous names are hidden from attendees. - **Polls**: prepared on the webinar page, launched and ended from the room, results shared or kept private. Single or multiple choice. - **Raise hand**: the host sees hands first in the People list and can lower them.

title: Webinars: Setup and limits
text: - Module **Webinars** (Admin Console, Modules) and the plan entitlement **Allow webinars** (off on Basic, on for paid plans and admins; per user in Admin). - Admin Console, Meeting platforms, *Webinars*: `webinar_max_attendees` (default 500) and `webinar_mesh_max` (default 40). - Emails use the system mail sender. Reminders run from the background worker every minute (day before, hour before, optional automatic follow-up). - Large audiences need the Cloudflare Realtime video server (SFU) configured. Webinars use it automatically. Without it, video is peer to peer and the number of watchers is capped by `webinar_mesh_max`.

title: Webinars: Not tested here
text: - Delivery to hundreds of simultaneous viewers through the real Cloudflare server. - Real email delivery (tests capture the emails). - Browser behaviour beyond Chromium with fake camera and microphone.

title: isiftmail: How it fits together
text: ``` iSift (this app) --IMAP 993 / SMTP 587 / ManageSieve 4190--> Stalwart mail server (your VPS) --outbound relay--> the internet | ^ +---------- management address (HTTPS): create / close mailbox | the internet --port 25 (incoming mail)---------------------------------+ ``` * **Stalwart** stores the mail, receives mail from the internet and filters spam. * **iSift** shows the mailbox (it reads and sends over IMAP and SMTP, like any other Commbox account) and manages mailboxes through Stalwart's management address. * **The outbound relay** (a sending service such as Amazon SES, Mailgun or Postmark) delivers outgoing mail, so Gmail, Hotmail and Yahoo accept it from a brand-new server. Stalwart is set to pass outgoing mail to the relay; iSift never holds the relay's login. You can remove the relay later if your own server earns a good reputation.

title: isiftmail: 1. The server (one small VPS)
text: * A VPS with 2 GB RAM / 20 GB disk is enough for a pilot; 4 GB for a few hundred people. Choose a host that **allows outbound port 25** (confirm with their support before you pay; AWS, Google Cloud and some budget hosts block it) and gives you **reverse DNS (PTR)** control. * Install **Stalwart Mail Server version 0.15.x** (Docker or the installer from stalw.art). iSift's management calls use the REST `/api/principal` interface of 0.15 and earlier. Newer Stalwart versions moved account management to JMAP; if you install a newer one, only `backend/app/integrations/isiftmail.py` needs changing. * In Stalwart: add your domain (for example `isiftmail.com`), turn on automatic TLS certificates (ACME) for `mail.isiftmail.com`, create an administrator account for iSift, and keep the spam filter on. * Open ports: 25 (incoming mail), 587 and 465 (sending), 993 (reading), 443 (management and web admin), 4190 (ManageSieve, for auto-reply). Port 4190 only needs to be reachable from the machine that runs iSift: firewall it to that address.

title: isiftmail: 2. DNS (at your domain registrar)
text: | Record | Name | Value | |---|---|---| | A | `mail.isiftmail.com` | the VPS address | | MX | `isiftmail.com` | `mail.isiftmail.com` (priority 10) | | TXT (SPF) | `isiftmail.com` | `v=spf1 mx include:<your relay's SPF> -all` (the relay tells you the exact include) | | TXT (DKIM) | `<selector>._domainkey.isiftmail.com` | the key Stalwart shows for the domain (and the relay's own DKIM records, if it asks for them) | | TXT (DMARC) | `_dmarc.isiftmail.com` | `v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:postmaster@isiftmail.com` | | PTR (reverse DNS) | the VPS address | `mail.isiftmail.com` (set at the VPS host) | Check the result at mail-tester.com before you invite anyone.

title: isiftmail: 3. The outbound relay
text: 1. Make an account with the relay service, verify `isiftmail.com` there, and get its SMTP host, port and login. 2. In Stalwart, add that service as the **remote relay** and send every non-local recipient through it (Stalwart's "queue / outbound next-hop" and "remote relay" settings; the names differ slightly between versions, so follow the relay section of the Stalwart documentation for your version). 3. Send a test message from a mailbox to a Gmail address and confirm it arrives in the inbox, not Spam. Cost guide: one VPS about A$8 to A$25 a month, the domain about A$20 a year, a relay about A$1 per 10,000 messages.

title: isiftmail: 4. Tell iSift (Admin Console)
text: **Admin Console > API and Settings > Email and calendar > isiftmail (our own email service)**: | Setting | Example | |---|---| | Address domain | `isiftmail.com` | | Mail server management address | `https://mail.isiftmail.com` | | Administrator name / password or token | the Stalwart administrator you made (leave the name empty to use a token) | | Mailbox (IMAP) server / port | `mail.isiftmail.com` / 993 | | Sending (SMTP) server / port | `mail.isiftmail.com` / 587 | | Auto-reply (ManageSieve) port | 4190 | | Mailbox size for each person | 2048 MB | | Mail (MX) name for people's own domains | `mail.isiftmail.com` (empty = the IMAP server) | | SPF record shown for people's own domains | `v=spf1 mx include:<your relay's SPF include> ~all` | The same values can come from the environment: `ISIFTMAIL_DOMAIN`, `ISIFTMAIL_API_URL`, `ISIFTMAIL_API_USER`, `ISIFTMAIL_API_PASSWORD`, `ISIFTMAIL_IMAP_HOST`, `ISIFTMAIL_IMAP_PORT`, `ISIFTMAIL_SMTP_HOST`, `ISIFTMAIL_SMTP_PORT`, `ISIFTMAIL_SIEVE_PORT`, `ISIFTMAIL_QUOTA_MB`, `ISIFTMAIL_MX_HOST`, `ISIFTMAIL_SPF`. The on/off switch is **Admin Console > Customers > Modules > Commbox: isiftmail**. It can also be left out of a plan under **Customers > Plans**. Turned off, the offer disappears and the isiftmail routes refuse requests; people who already have an address keep their mail on the server.

title: isiftmail: Who can have an address
text: Anyone who can use Commbox. (Commbox's own plan rule still applies: the Basic plan has no Commbox unless an administrator allows it. To open isiftmail to Basic customers as well, allow Commbox for that plan under Customers > Plans.) A person has **one free address** on your isiftmail domain; the administrator can make more. Closed addresses are held back for 180 days so nobody can take over mail meant for the previous owner.

title: isiftmail: Own domains (pramod@prama-ai.com)
text: In **Commbox > Mail > Use my own domain** a person: 1. **Adds the domain** (for example `prama-ai.com`). iSift shows the DNS records to add where the domain is managed (GoDaddy, Cloudflare, and so on): an **ownership TXT** record, the **MX** record, **SPF**, **DKIM** (shown once the domain is verified) and **DMARC**. 2. **Presses Check my DNS.** iSift looks the records up on the internet. When the ownership record is found the domain is **verified**: only then is it set up on the mail server and can mailboxes be made on it. Nobody can hold a domain they do not control, and if two people add the same domain the one who proves it first keeps it. Mail only arrives once the MX record is in place, and the page says so. 3. **Makes mailboxes**: their own (`pramod@prama-ai.com`) and, like the Microsoft 365 admin centre, **for team members**: give the member's iSift sign-in email and the mailbox appears in their Mail (right away if they have an account, or the first time they sign in). The domain owner can **reset the password** and **close** any mailbox on their domain, see which are waiting, and remove the domain once no mailbox is left on it. Up to 3 domains per person and 50 mailboxes per domain. The reserved-names list applies only to the free isiftmail domain: `info@` and `postmaster@` are fine on your own domain. On the mail server each mailbox on a person's own domain has the login name `name.domain-with-dashes` (for example `pramod.prama-ai-com`), so two companies can both have `info@`. People never need it: iSift stores the login and password. They are shown (once) only fo

title: isiftmail: Outlook, Thunderbird and phone auto-setup
text: For a person's own domain iSift also shows three more records (recommended, and checked by **Check my DNS**): `autodiscover.<domain>` and `autoconfig.<domain>` (both CNAMEs to the **Auto-setup name** in Admin Console) and an `_autodiscover._tcp.<domain>` SRV record. With them, Outlook, Thunderbird and phones set themselves up from just the address and password. iSift answers the requests itself, with no sign-in: `/autodiscover/autodiscover.xml` (Outlook) and `/mail/config-v1.1.xml` (Thunderbird, phones), only for your isiftmail domain and for verified own domains. Two things you must do on the server side: * The **Auto-setup name** (setting `isiftmail_autoconfig_host`, default is the mail name) must be a name with a valid HTTPS certificate that reaches those two addresses, for example your reverse proxy forwarding them to the iSift app. * Outlook connects to `https://autodiscover.<their-domain>/...`, and a CNAME cannot give that name a certificate for the customer's domain. Outlook therefore follows the SRV record and asks the person once to **allow the redirect** to your Auto-setup name. That prompt is normal. Without it, people still can set up by hand from the server details iSift shows.

title: isiftmail: Easy setup, for people and for you
text: * **Free address:** the person sees a few free names made from their own name, taps one, and the address is in their Mail. Nothing to type. * **Own domain:** iSift looks up where the domain is managed (GoDaddy, Cloudflare, Namecheap and others) and says where to click, offers **Copy all records**, and re-checks the DNS every 20 seconds by itself while the window is open, showing how many records are found. When the ownership record appears, the domain verifies and mailboxes can be made. (One-click connection to a registrar's account is not built in.) * **Phone and Outlook:** **Use this address on your phone or in Outlook** gives iPhone, iPad and Mac a one-tap profile (a `.mobileconfig` that contains the mailbox password, made only for the signed-in person). Outlook and Android find their settings from the address (see auto-setup above). * **You, the administrator:** in Admin Console, API and Settings, Email and calendar, press **Test my mail server**. It checks the management login, the IMAP, SMTP and auto-reply ports, and your MX, SPF and DMARC records, and says in plain words what to fix.

title: isiftmail: What people get
text: Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Junk and Deleted folders; reading, replying, forwarding, deleting and moving; **Save draft** and **Edit draft** (isiftmail addresses); a **signature** added to new messages; an **auto-reply** with optional start and end dates (a Sieve "vacation" rule on the server, once a day per sender); a **new password** for using the mailbox in Outlook or a phone app; and **Close this mailbox**. Each address has its own signature and auto-reply. Spam filtering is Stalwart's built-in filter; "Junk" in Commbox moves a message to the Junk folder.

title: isiftmail: Spam control (built in)
text: Open sign-up invites spam senders, so iSift limits and watches every isiftmail mailbox. The numbers are in Admin Console under the isiftmail settings: * **Sending limits** per mailbox: messages per hour (30), per day (200; a mailbox under a day old gets a quarter of that) and people in one message (50). Over a limit, iSift refuses the message and says when to try again. * **New addresses**: a person can open only one free address, and one network address can open only a few a day (default 3, times 3 signed-in people). * **Automatic suspension**: after 3 spam complaints or 20 hard bounces a mailbox is suspended. Its password on the mail server is replaced (so nobody, including Outlook or a phone, can send or read) and iSift refuses to send from it. An administrator restores it in **Customers > Mailboxes**, which also lists every mailbox with messages sent in 24 hours, complaints and bounces, and has Suspend and Restore buttons. Restoring puts the original password back and clears the counters. Every suspension is in the audit log. * **Complaint and bounce notices from your outbound relay.** Set **Secret for relay complaint and bounce notices** in Admin Console, then give your relay this address as its webhook (for example an Amazon SES notification or any relay webhook): `https://<your iSift address>/api/v1/isiftmail/hooks/relay?secret=<the secret>` iSift reads a list `{"events":[{"type":"complaint","from":"name@isiftmail.com"}]}` or one event, and the usual relay shapes (`notificationType`, `mail.source`, `bounceType`). Temporary bounces are ignored. Without the secret the

title: isiftmail: Before you open it to the public
text: * Test with 3 or 4 people first, including sending to and from Gmail, Outlook.com and Yahoo. * Limit abuse: switch on the relay notices above, check Customers > Mailboxes weekly, and set sending limits on the mail server too. * Back up the Stalwart data folder daily and test a restore. * Add the mail terms to your Terms of Use and Privacy Policy (you store people's messages), and comply with the Spam Act 2003. * What has not been tested here: the connection to a real Stalwart server or real DNS. The management calls (including the domain ones), ManageSieve, IMAP draft saving and the DNS lookups were tested against stand-ins, so run the checks above on your server, with one real domain, before announcing it. * Letting anyone open an address makes your domain a target for spam senders. The built-in limits and suspension (above) reduce it but do not replace watching your relay's reports.

title: Give control of a shared file
text: Share a PDF or photo through iSift (More, Share a file), then choose Give control to and pick a participant. They can move through pages and scroll the file for everyone. The host can take control back at any time, and only the host can stop sharing. This works for files shared through iSift, not for a whole screen or for a PowerPoint or Word file on the host's computer; save those as PDF first.
